predecessors.name: Kediri Kingdom
predecessors.text: Jayakatwang's Kediri, overthrown by the Yuan expedition and Raden Wijaya in 1293

successors.text: Daha and the Java core, taken by Demak: 'defeating Daha in 1518'

successors.name: Blambangan Kingdom
successors.text: the east of East Java, Blambangan

successors.name: Balinese Kingdom (Gelgel)
successors.text: Bali: courtiers and priests 'fled east to Bali'

ledger.x: 1294: the Java realm of Singhasari is Majapahit's.
1352: the Malay Peninsula as Majapahit's sphere.
ledger.cp: Malay Peninsula principalities (Pahang, Kelantan, Terengganu, Johor)

ledger.x: 1352: south and central Sumatra as Majapahit's sphere.
1355: the third invasion of Nan Sarunai.
1365: the eastern sphere is written down.
1377: the rebellion in Palembang is put down in the same year ('punitive naval attack'); the page gives no later date.
1403: the east of East Java breaks away.
1406: the east of East Java returns to the Western court.
1406: the outer sphere falls away after the Regreg War.

1468: Kertabhumi rebels and the court retreats to Daha.
1478: Demak declares itself independent 'In response to the collapse of Kertabhumi of Trowulan and the rise of Girindrawardhana of Daha in 1478' and stops paying tribute.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Java
wars.outcome: Majapahit is founded in the aftermath: Kublai Khan 'sent a massive expedition of 30,000 soldiers and 1,000 ships to Java' against Singhasari's successors, and Raden Wijaya founded his stronghold the same year.

wars.name: Majapahit conquest of Bali
wars.outcome: Majapahit victory: Bedulu captured in 1343 after seven months of battles; a vassal dynasty placed on Bali; Lombok conquered the same year.

wars.name: Majapahit invasion of Samudera Pasai
wars.outcome: Pasai attacked and looted (Hikayat Raja Pasai: a naval invasion of 1350); no annexation is stated.

wars.name: Majapahit attack on Singapura (1350)
wars.outcome: Repulsed: 'a failed attempt to take Singapore in 1350'.

wars.name: Battle of Bubat
wars.outcome: The Sunda king and his family, come to marry his daughter to Hayam Wuruk, are killed in a skirmish at Bubat square; Sunda is not annexed ('the only remaining state refusing to acknowledge Majapahit's hegemony', Gajah Mada page).

wars.name: Majapahit invasions of Nan Sarunai
wars.outcome: Third invasion launched 1355, battles in April 1358 and December 1362; Negara Dipa founded 'under Majapahit tributary'.

wars.name: Majapahit punitive expedition to Palembang
wars.outcome: A rebellion put down by a punitive naval attack in 1377.

wars.name: Majapahit sack of Singapura (1398)
wars.outcome: Singapura sacked and destroyed after a siege; Parameswara flees to found Malacca in 1400.

wars.name: Regreg War
wars.outcome: Majapahit (Western court) victory; the Eastern court reunited; the outer vassals slip away afterwards.

wars.name: Kertabhumi's rebellion and the Sudarma Wisuta war
wars.outcome: 'In 1468 Prince Kertabhumi rebelled against Singhawikramawardhana, promoting himself as the king of Majapahit'; in 1478, 'the year of Sudarma Wisuta war', Ranawijaya's army under general Udara 'breached Trowulan defences and killed Kertabumi in his palace'.

wars.name: Demak-Majapahit conflicts
wars.outcome: Demak independent from 1478 and 'consolidate[s] its power by defeating Daha in 1518'; the Majapahit page has the final fall in 1527.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line exists on the pages: the Java frontier with Sunda is approximate, and the overseas sphere is a tint of claimed tribute, not a boundary; the island coasts of Java, Bali and Lombok are natural limits.
